# Overview

`MiR_Score()` performs miRNA enrichment analysis by testing whether a
pathway's miRNAs are located unexpectedly toward one end of a ranked
miRNA list. The ranked list covers every miRNA in `mir_DEdata`, ranked
by each miRNA's own differential expression statistic. This is a GSEA
style test, built on `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("clusterProfiler")`'s
`GSEA()`. Note that unlike `TG_Score()`, the ranked list here is not
restricted through `background_MGI`, only the pathway side is.

This vignette uses the same toy BLCA example data as the package's main
Quick Start vignette. See `vignette("miREA")` for a description of that
data and for running all nine methods together through `miREA()`.

# Required inputs

* `pathway`, a two column data frame with columns `pathway` and `gene`.
* `mir_DEdata`, a four column data frame with columns `miRNA`,
  `log2FoldChange`, `stat`, and `padj`.
* `background_MGI`, a two column data frame with columns `miRNA` and
  `gene`, or `NULL` to use the bundled default (see `vignette("miREA")`,
  Step 1, for details on `background_MGI`). This is used to derive the
  pathway miRNA set `MiR_Score()` tests against, since pathway
  definitions only specify genes.
* `pvalueType` for `MiR_Score()` itself, one of `"pos"`, `"neg"`, or
  `"std"`, selecting a one sided or two sided test.

```{r load-data}
library(miREA)
data(toy_pathway)
data(toy_mir_DEdata)
data(toy_gene_DEdata)
data(background_MGI)
```

# Run MiR-Score

```{r prepare-input}
input_data <- getAllInputData(
    methods = "MiR_Score",
    pathway = toy_pathway,
    mir_DEdata = toy_mir_DEdata,
    gene_DEdata = toy_gene_DEdata,
    background_MGI = background_MGI
)
```

`input_data$data$MiR_Score` holds the ranked miRNA list, covering every
miRNA in `toy_mir_DEdata`, ranked by its own differential expression
statistic. `input_data$pathway$MiR` holds the pathway miRNA sets, derived
from `toy_pathway`'s genes through `background_MGI`.

```{r run-mir-score}
res <- MiR_Score(
    miRList = input_data$data$MiR_Score,
    pathway = input_data$pathway$MiR,
    pvalueType = "std",
    pvalueCutoff = 1
)
head(res)
```

# Run through miREA()

`MiR_Score()` can also be run through the `miREA()` wrapper, which is
useful when you want its result alongside other methods' results in a
single `miREAResult` object (see `vignette("miREA")`, Step 2, for the
multi-method case). `MiR_Score()` itself has no `background` argument,
but `miREA()` still requires one for the `MiR` target, since `MiR_ORA()`
shares that target and does use it. For a single target, `background`
can be a plain character vector instead of a named list.

```{r run-through-miREA}
result <- miREA(
    methods = "MiR_Score",
    input_data = input_data,
    background = unique(input_data$pathway$MiR$miRNA),
    pvalueCutoff = 1
)
head(result$result$MiR_Score)
```

# Supplying your own ranked miRNA list

If you already have a ranked miRNA list from an external analysis
instead of letting `getAllInputData()` derive one from `mir_DEdata`, call
`MiR_Score()` directly with that list and `input_data$pathway$MiR`.
`miRList` must be a named numeric vector, sorted from the highest to the
lowest score.

```{r custom-list, eval=FALSE}
my_miRList <- sort(c(`hsa-miR-21-5p` = 2.3, `hsa-miR-155-5p` = -1.1), decreasing = TRUE)
res_custom <- MiR_Score(
    miRList = my_miRList,
    pathway = input_data$pathway$MiR,
    pvalueType = "std",
    pvalueCutoff = 1
)
```
